canonical_statement: Let X be a real-valued random variable on a probability space with finite second moment. For every real r > 0, the probability that |X - E[X]| is at least r is at most Var(X) / r^2.
domain_and_universes: Provisional: a measurable sample type Omega, a probability measure mu on Omega, X : Omega -> Real, and r : Real; exact universe and typeclass binders remain open.
ordered_quantifiers: mu : Measure Omega with IsProbabilityMeasure mu
X : Omega -> Real with the exact measurability and finite-second-moment hypotheses
hypotheses: X is measurable in the sense required by the selected mathlib expectation/variance API
X has a finite second moment (exact Lean predicate to be frozen)
conclusion: mu {omega | r <= abs (X omega - E_mu[X])} <= Var_mu(X) / r^2, after selecting and checking the exact probability-valued coercions.

alternate_encodings.target: P(|X - E[X]| >= k * sigma) <= 1 / k^2 for k > 0
alternate_encodings.relationship: Equivalent when sigma is a finite positive standard deviation; sigma = 0 needs a separate checked boundary argument.
Equivalent for r > 0 after a pointwise event equality.

excluded_or_degenerate_cases: r = 0 and r < 0 are outside the canonical quantified threshold
variables without a finite second moment are outside scope
one-sided Cantelli bounds and deterministic Chebyshev sum inequalities are different theorems
